oidc_jwt.description: JWT login is a stateless signature-and-claims verification flow; the documentation does not describe jti tracking or one-time JWT consumption.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same valid JWT may succeed by design; do not flag replay_same_token or missing jti tracking as a vulnerability for this flow.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name may include an auth mount prefix before the upstream identity value.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/token.mdx lookup-self sample response shows display_name like ldap2-tesla
oidc_jwt.note: Treat mount-prefixed display names as normal platform formatting, not identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias name, which can cause privilege sharing through alias reuse.
oidc_jwt.note: This is documented as a security consideration, not necessarily a product bug. Collision findings must distinguish documented alias reuse behavior from unintended identity collapse.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider metadata declares request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false.
oidc_jwt.note: Unsigned request-object attacks are not applicable to this provider surface because request objects are not supported.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider supports only the authorization_code grant and code response type in discovery metadata.
oidc_jwt.note: Failures for implicit, hybrid, or token-exchange style requests are by design.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC provider or named key with empty allowed_client_ids allows no clients, not all clients.
oidc_jwt.note: Empty allowlists causing login denial are by design.

oidc_jwt.description: OIDC clients deny all Vault entities by default unless assignments are configured; allow_all must be set explicitly to permit everyone.
oidc_jwt.note: Authentication failures through an unassigned client are expected behavior, not authorization bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider does not support request or request_uri parameters.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag lack of request-object handling as acceptance of unsigned request objects; the feature is documented as unsupported.

oidc_jwt.constraint: configure_jwt_validation on /v1/auth/{mount}/config requires EXACTLY ONE trust source: oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. The fuzzer MUST NOT set more than one, and MUST set one of them, or setup is invalid.
configure_jwt_validation: bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. For issuer-validation tests, do NOT use jwks_pairs if the test needs bound_issuer enforcement.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on JWT roles, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. If omitted, Vault has no configured issuer value to compare against, so issuer-mismatch tests are invalid.
create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. A role with no bound constraints is invalid setup. For JWT roles, use at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims.

For JWT roles, if the JWT contains an aud claim (typical case), bound_audiences is required and the token aud must match at least one configured audience. Do not run audience-validation tests with a JWT role lacking bound_audiences when the token includes aud.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only; there is no companion bound_subject_type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting a wildcard.

bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching only; there is no companion type parameter. Wildcards are not documented. For cross-provider or multi-audience tests, configure explicit audience values; do NOT assume '*' matches anything.

bound_claims keys may use JSON pointer syntax, but value matching is controlled by bound_claims_type. If bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. If bound_claims_type='glob', '*' is wildcard. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple claim values to pass the same role, either omit the exact-match constraint or explicitly set bound_claims_type='glob'; do NOT set '*' under the default string mode.

bound_claims accepts string, integer, boolean, or list-of-strings expected values. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type='glob' rather than the default 'string' so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 is strict validation.
expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 is strict expiration enforcement.
not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 is strict nbf enforcement.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against JWT roles, include a CONTROL login using a valid token (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}) alongside the attack token. Otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may reflect broken setup rather than time-claim enforcement.

OIDC auth_url/client flow: public clients MUST use PKCE. The authorization endpoint documents code_challenge as required for public clients, and the token endpoint documents code_verifier as required for public clients and for codes granted using PKCE. Tests that omit PKCE on public clients should expect flow rejection, not identity differences.

OIDC auth_url/client flow: confidential clients may use PKCE optionally, but public clients must use client_id at the token endpoint because they have no client_secret. The fuzzer MUST align client_type, token endpoint auth method, and PKCE usage or failures are by design.

Vault's OIDC auth_url endpoint returns a Vault-generated auth_url rather than acting as a standard /authorize redirect endpoint. The fuzzer MUST treat start_oidc_auth as a JSON POST that yields data.auth_url, then drive the browser/IdP flow externally before calling /v1/auth/{mount}/oidc/callback.

OIDC callback coherence: /v1/auth/{mount}/oidc/callback requires state, nonce, and code, plus matching client_nonce if one was supplied to auth_url. For state-swap or code-injection tests, preserve the exact tuple generated for the same flow; mismatches are expected rejection, not evidence of a bug.

configure_jwt_validation default_role affects logins where no role is supplied. For jwt_default_role_change tests, the attack must omit role on login_with_jwt so the mount-level default_role is actually exercised.

JWT signing-key rotation tests must update the same trust source actually in use (jwks_url, oidc_discovery_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys). Changing an unused trust parameter does not affect validation and yields a false test.

create_identity_group supports type=internal or external. For JWT/OIDC external group mapping tests via group aliases, use external groups and map them with create_group_alias; manual member_entity_ids on a group does not test upstream group-claim binding.

Group alias mapping depends on the auth mount accessor. The fuzzer MUST obtain the accessor for the JWT/OIDC auth mount and use that exact mount_accessor when creating group aliases, or group-claim mapping tests are invalid.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive in Vault: multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby gain the alias's privileges. For I4 collision tests, alias reuse is a documented risk surface, so the fuzzer should prefer unique alias values except when intentionally testing collisions.
KV v2 verify_read_secret MUST use the /data/ path segment: /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and causes false 404s unrelated to authorization.

KV v2 list operations use /metadata/ paths, and the docs explicitly state list capability must be granted on /metadata/ even if reads/writes use /data/. If a test needs listing, policy must include metadata paths separately.

KV v2 engine config has sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 does NOT mean keep zero versions; it means use the default of 10 versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion timer. Never interpret these as literal zero-retention or immediate deletion.

Vault token use budgets: token num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Any nonzero use budget is consumed by EVERY API call made with that session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the fuzzer needs both a self-lookup and a secret-read in one sequence, the minimum safe value is 2; if it also performs entity lookups, increase accordingly.

Vault-issued OIDC provider clients default to allowing no entities via assignments. The client docs state that by default no Vault entities are allowed, and allow_all must be supplied to allow all entities. For provider-side OIDC tests, create_application MUST set assignments appropriately or authorization failures are by design.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids semantics: empty means no clients are allowed; '*' means all clients are allowed. Never treat empty as wildcard. For cross-client authorization tests, configure explicit allowed_client_ids or '*'.

OIDC provider redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, ensure the baseline uses an exact configured URI; otherwise failures are expected setup errors.

OIDC provider discovery explicitly advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run request-object or request_uri based OIDC tests against Vault's provider endpoints; rejection or lack of support is by design.

OIDC provider discovery advertises grant_types_supported=['authorization_code'] only. Do NOT attempt RFC 8693 token_exchange against /v1/identity/oidc/provider/{name}/token; token exchange is not documented for this endpoint.

UserInfo endpoint requires Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. For provider-side OIDC tests, session_token must be the access_token from /token, not the id_token. Using id_token as Bearer will invalidate identity verification.
OIDC provider authorization endpoint requires scope to include openid. Tests omitting openid are invalid setup, not security findings.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST set bound_issuer. The docs mark bound_issuer optional; if omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim, so issuer-substitution tests become meaningless.

bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. Do not use jwks_pairs for issuer-enforcement tests that need bound_issuer; use oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys instead.

For JWT roles, if the JWT contains an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and the JWT aud must match at least one configured audience. Do not run audience-mismatch or empty-audience tests without first establishing a control role/token pair where aud matches bound_audiences.

bound_claims supports two matching modes controlled by bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type='string' means literal exact matching; glob wildcards are NOT active unless bound_claims_type='glob'. For multi-identity tests, do not set bound_claims values to '*' unless bound_claims_type is explicitly set to 'glob'.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on bound_claims, set bound_claims_type='glob' rather than the default 'string'. The docs state default string mode treats values as literals and must match exactly, while glob mode interprets values as globs; use glob mode so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings instead of being rejected outright.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric type coercion by configuring an integer bound_claims value N and sending a JWT claim with float N+0.7. If Vault truncates/coerces and matches silently, that is an I5 issue.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. If the selected claim is absent or non-string, alias creation/login will fail for reasons unrelated to the invariant under test. For I4 tests, use a string-valued claim such as sub or another stable string claim.
groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. Sending groups as a bare string instead of an array is invalid setup and can confound I4/I5 group-mapping tests.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, while value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict zero-skew enforcement.
expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, while value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means immediate expiration enforcement.
not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, while value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict nbf enforcement.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against JWT auth, include a CONTROL login using a valid token alongside the attack token. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken trust configuration, wrong role setup, or invalid claim mapping.

For I3 config-change tests (role tighten, signing key rotation, default_role change, bound_issuer change), the second login must be a NEW login request after the admin update. A changed outcome for a new login after config mutation is the expected test oracle; do not treat the admin change itself as a flow-coherence bug.

OIDC callback on /v1/auth/{mount}/oidc/callback requires state, nonce, and code from the same auth_url flow, plus matching client_nonce if one was supplied earlier. Do not mix values across sessions; state/nonce swaps are invalid setup unless intentionally testing session binding.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request and OIDC callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault's OIDC provider authorization endpoint requires scope to include 'openid'. Requests without openid are invalid OIDC setup, not authorization-binding findings.

For Vault OIDC provider tests, redirect_uri must EXACTLY match one of the client's configured redirect_uris at authorization time, and the same redirect_uri must be sent again to the token endpoint. Do not vary redirect_uri between authorize and token steps except when intentionally testing redirect_uri_mismatch.

Vault OIDC provider clients default to allowing NO entities unless assignments are configured. To permit authentication through a client, set assignments explicitly; to allow all entities, use the built-in allow_all assignment. Otherwise login failures are by design and will look like auth bugs.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: allowed_client_ids on OIDC providers and named keys has exact-list semantics with a special '*' wildcard meaning all clients. Empty means NO clients are allowed. Do not interpret empty as unrestricted.

Public OIDC clients MUST use PKCE for the authorization code flow. Confidential clients may use PKCE optionally. For public-client control flows, include code_challenge at authorize and code_verifier at token exchange; missing verifier failures are by design, not I3 bugs.

Vault OIDC provider discovery advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT attempt request-object tests (including alg=none request JWTs) against this provider endpoint; unsupported request parameters would yield false positives.

For OIDC SSO/id_token validation strategy, always send and verify nonce in the authorization request because Vault's provider docs only strongly encourage it rather than making it mandatory. A missing nonce weakens replay testing and can make I2 results ambiguous.
verify_read_secret for KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment: /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits the wrong API shape and returns misleading 404s.
KV v2 list operations use /metadata/ paths, not /data/. If policies are intended to permit listing, grant list capability on /metadata/ as documented; otherwise list failures are by design.

KV v2 engine config max_versions has sentinel semantics: value 0 does NOT mean keep zero versions; it means use the default retention of 10 versions. Do not use 0 when testing immediate version eviction.
KV v2 delete_version_after has sentinel semantics: value '0s' means versions are not automatically deleted. Do not assume '0s' means immediate deletion.
oidc_jwt.source: kv-v2 Configure the KV engine and metadata docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Token use-budget parameters consume uses on EVERY API call made with that token, including verify_granted_identity (/auth/token/lookup-self) and verify_read_secret. If a role or token is configured with num_uses/token_num_uses=1, lookup-self will exhaust the token before the access test. Minimum safe value for a sequence that does both verification and secret read is at least 2.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/token lookup-self and token fields in role docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Identity group type matters: external groups are intended to receive memberships via aliases from auth methods, while internal groups can have member_entity_ids set directly. For JWT/OIDC external-group mapping tests, create the group as type='external' and use create_group_alias rather than manual member_entity_ids.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive. Vault docs explicitly warn that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby gain all its privileges. For I4 collision tests, treat alias reuse as a real risk surface and ensure each control identity normally gets a unique alias value.

Group policy application mode can be 'within_namespace_hierarchy' or 'any'. In Enterprise, if mode='any', group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy and may look like over-granting. Check /v1/sys/config/group-policy-application before flagging cross-namespace group-policy escalation.

configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source: set ONE AND ONLY ONE of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do not send multiple trust-anchor sources in the same config or the setup is invalid.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer when using oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim against a configured issuer value, so issuer-substitution tests become meaningless. Also note bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set.

Numeric sentinel semantics: on JWT roles, clock_skew_leeway value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. expiration_leeway value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. not_before_leeway value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict checking.

JWT roles require at least one bound value to be set. A valid role setup must include at least one constraint such as bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims; otherwise role creation/update is invalid.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only. There is no companion bound_subject_type parameter. Wildcards such as '*' are treated literally, not as patterns. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple sub values to pass the same role, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to a wildcard.

Claim value type handling: bound_claims accepts string, integer, boolean, or list of strings, but the default bound_claims_type=string treats values as literals and must match exactly. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type=glob rather than the default string so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings instead of being rejected outright.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. For I4 type-confusion tests, a non-string user_claim or non-list groups_claim is invalid setup and may be rejected before alias/group mapping occurs.

user_claim and bound_claims keys support JSON pointer syntax only when configured accordingly. user_claim_json_pointer defaults to false, so a slash-containing value is not automatically treated as a JSON pointer. For tests targeting nested claims, explicitly enable user_claim_json_pointer for user_claim and use documented JSON-pointer syntax for bound_claims keys.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on JWT roles, include a CONTROL login using a valid token in the same setup. Because leeway defaults are nonzero (60s/150s), an attack token near the boundary may still succeed by design; use timestamps well outside the configured leeway or set leeways to -1 for strict tests.

For I3 config-change tests, re-logins after modify_role_config or configure_jwt_validation are expected to use the NEW configuration immediately. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same credential before and after the admin change, not treat the admin change itself as a bug.

OIDC callback flow coherence: the callback requires state, nonce, and code, and client_nonce must match the value previously supplied to oidc/auth_url if used. For I3 state/nonce swap tests, preserve the exact auth_url-issued state/nonce tuple per session; cross-session mixing is the attack, not a setup shortcut.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request and OIDC callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault's JWT/OIDC auth_url endpoint is POST /auth/{mount}/oidc/auth_url, not a standard GET /authorize endpoint. The executor must first obtain Vault's generated auth_url and then drive the upstream browser redirect separately; do not synthesize your own authorize request against Vault for this auth method.

OIDC provider authorization endpoint requires scope to include openid, supports only response_type=code, and PKCE is required for public clients but optional for confidential clients. For PKCE tests, choose client_type accordingly; missing code_verifier on a public client is expected to fail by design.

OIDC provider token endpoint supports only grant_type=authorization_code. Do not attempt RFC 8693 token_exchange against /v1/identity/oidc/provider/{name}/token; token exchange is not documented for this provider endpoint.

OIDC provider discovery explicitly reports request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do not run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against Vault's documented OIDC provider authorization endpoint; unsigned request objects are unsupported rather than accepted.

OIDC provider discovery reports token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported as client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, and none. Public clients use none and must use PKCE; confidential clients may use client_secret_basic or client_secret_post. Test expectations must account for client_type-specific authentication behavior at the token endpoint.

Numeric sentinel semantics for OIDC provider/client TTLs are documented as defaults, not disable flags. client id_token_ttl and access_token_ttl default to 24h if omitted. Do not assume zero disables token lifetime unless explicitly documented; use explicit durations for deterministic I2 tests.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids semantics: empty allowed_client_ids means NO clients are allowed; '*' means all clients are allowed. For I5 audience/client-authorization tests, distinguish empty from wildcard because empty is deny-all, not unconstrained allow.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC client assignments semantics: by default, no Vault entities are allowed to authenticate through a client. To allow all entities, explicitly assign the built-in allow_all assignment. Tests that expect successful authorization code flow must configure assignments accordingly.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, a mismatch is expected to fail by design and should be asserted via error status rather than identity comparison.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: Session-use budget: token num_uses limits every API call made with that Vault session, including verify_granted_identity via /auth/token/lookup-self and verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value is 2 if the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read after login; use 3+ if additional session-authenticated inspection calls are included.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/token lookup-self docs and fuzzer execution context

oidc_jwt.constraint: Group alias creation for JWT/OIDC group mapping requires the auth mount accessor of the JWT/OIDC auth method. The provided docs do not include a documented sys/auth mount-accessor endpoint for JWT mounts; without an accessor source, create_group_alias cannot be executed reliably from these docs alone.

External identity groups are populated through aliases from auth methods. For JWT/OIDC group-policy tests, create an external group and bind it with create_group_alias rather than manually relying on member_entity_ids to simulate upstream group claims.

Enterprise-only global group policy mode affects authorization results: default within_namespace_hierarchy applies group policies only when the request token is created in the same namespace hierarchy; mode any applies group policies regardless of namespace hierarchy. Cross-namespace group-policy escalation tests must account for this global setting or they may produce false positives.
